sources.title: HD3SS6126 USB 3.0 and USB 2.0 Differential Switch 2:1/1:2 MUX/DEMUX datasheet
sources.revision: SLAS975A; November 2013, revised August 2015; package outline RUA0042A dated 03/2020; live package addendum observed 2026-02-06
observed_facts: RUA WQFN package has 42 signal pins and nominal body 9.00 x 3.50 mm
generic package view specifies 0.50 mm pitch and 0.8 mm maximum height
package outline body limits are 8.9-9.1 mm by 3.4-3.6 mm and height 0.6-0.8 mm
TI example land pattern calls out 42 lands at 0.6 mm and 0.25 mm land width, with 38X and 42X 0.5 mm callouts
exposed thermal pad is package pad 43 and must be soldered to the PCB
TI example land pattern shows 0.2 mm typical vias, optional by application
TI recommends vias under paste be filled, plugged, or tented
TI example stencil is based on 0.125 mm thickness and 69% printed solder coverage under the package
active orderable HD3SS6126RUAR and HD3SS6126RUARG4 are WQFN RUA 42-pin parts, 3000 per large tape and reel, MSL Level 3 at 260 C peak for 168 hours

sources.title: MEG-Array High Speed Mezzanine Connectors
sources.revision: GS-20-033 Rev J; verified 2016-04-27; printed 2016-05-04; retrieved 2026-09-12
observed_facts: unrestricted FCI application specification for MEG-Array BGA connector application and process guidance
400-position 10 x 40, 4.0 mm mated-height receptacle is 74221 with plug 84740
drawing and product specification take precedence if application guidance conflicts with them
recommended PCB pad diameter is 0.584 to 0.635 mm with copper-defined pads
solder-mask opening must provide at least 0.15 mm clearance around the pad
vias should not be included in BGA solder pads; connector-side via must be fully solder-mask covered
5.10 mm perimeter keepout is generally recommended for rework equipment
A1 is identified by a triangle and connector keying controls mating orientation
the document reports 4 mm and 6 mm stack-height testing to 28 Gb/s, a performance datum rather than a PiSXMe guarantee

sources.title: TUSB9261 Flash Burner
sources.publisher: Texas Instruments E2E / Jorge Llamas (TI expert response)
sources.revision: Thread 538818; response retrieved 2026-09-13; original thread over 9 years old
observed_facts: TUSB9261 EVM is not required for SPI programming if the image is correctly programmed
the SLLC416 firmware binary lacks the header needed for device recognition
FlashBurner SLLC414 can generate a formatted image for other SPI programming methods
SATA TX polarity in the image must match the board routing
